_comment: Lens table for the PR review gate. The triage job chooses lens IDS ONLY;
this file decides what each one costs. Keeping model/effort/turns here and
not in the model's output means a reviewer cannot vote itself more compute.
max_turns is a RUNAWAY BACKSTOP, not a budget. konyklabs/roadmap#16 exists
because the old gate's cap of 30 sat at the top of its own demand
distribution, so the tail failed with no verdict at all.
Measured on konyklabs/vendorfake#17, a large real diff:
lens         model   cap   used   outcome
deep         opus    120   77     completed
adversarial  opus    120   65     completed
broad        sonnet  100   101    error_max_turns, no verdict
history      sonnet   60   61     error_max_turns, no verdict
And on konyklabs/vendorfake#14, the same run:
triage       opus    40    54     rejected, over the configured maximum
Triage is not in this table — its budget lives in the workflow — but it has
the same failure mode and was missed in the first correction. Note the shape:
the model FINISHED (subtype success, is_error false) and the action rejected
the result anyway for exceeding the cap. max_turns is a hard refusal, not a
truncation, so a cap set near demand throws away completed work.
Both failures were the Sonnet lenses, and both landed at exactly cap+1 —
which means the true demand is unknown, only that it exceeded the cap.
Sonnet takes smaller steps than Opus and needs MORE headroom, not less;
the original caps assumed the opposite. Caps below are set well clear of
measured demand rather than just above it, and timeouts are raised to
match so a cap is never enforced by the clock instead.
